purpose: Dexchlorpheniramine is used to relieve allergy symptoms such as runny nose, sneezing, itchy or watery eyes, and skin itching or rashes. It can also help with symptoms from hay fever, hives, and other allergic reactions. Sometimes it is used to help relieve cold symptoms as well.
how_it_works: Your body releases a chemical called histamine when it reacts to something you are allergic to, and histamine is what causes those uncomfortable allergy symptoms. Dexchlorpheniramine works by blocking the histamine receptors in your body, so histamine cannot cause those symptoms. Think of it like putting a lock on a door so the histamine cannot get in and cause trouble.
common_side_effects: The most common side effect is drowsiness or feeling sleepy, which is very typical with this type of antihistamine. You may also notice a dry mouth, dry nose, or dry eyes. Some people feel dizzy, have blurred vision, feel a little confused, or have an upset stomach. Difficulty urinating or constipation can also occur.
warnings: Because this medication can make you very drowsy, do not drive a car, operate heavy machinery, or do anything that requires you to be fully alert until you know how it affects you. Avoid drinking alcohol while taking this medication as it can make the drowsiness much worse. Talk to your doctor before taking this if you have glaucoma, an enlarged prostate, breathing problems, or liver or kidney disease. It is not recommended for young children without a doctor's guidance and should be used with caution in older adults as it can increase the risk of falls and confusion.
typical_dosing: For adults and children 12 years and older, the usual dose is 2 mg every 4 to 6 hours as needed, not exceeding 12 mg in 24 hours. Extended-release tablets are typically 4 mg to 6 mg taken every 8 to 10 hours. For children aged 6 to 11 years, the usual dose is 1 mg every 4 to 6 hours. Always follow your doctor's or pharmacist's specific instructions, as dosing can vary by product and your individual needs.
